purpose: Report recorded token consumption for one project version and explain its distribution without changing lifecycle decisions.
requiredBehavior: Runtime owns deterministic collection, durable source ledger, explicit attribution, aggregation, snapshots, Markdown/JSON and its own Expert presentation.
Continuously collect available Codex usage from explicitly registered, read-only Host sources; do not copy model credentials or infer missing counts.
Retain original source identifiers, metric semantics, cursor/epoch, parent/fork lineage and evidence provenance; never retain unrelated prompt content merely for statistics.
Normalize cumulative observations to attributable deltas, deduplicate replays, handle out-of-order records, resets and inherited fork baselines without double counting.
Input/output totals and cached-input/reasoning-output subsets follow each actual source contract; never add inclusive subsets to totals again. Unknown values remain null.
Bind parallel tasks and source event ranges explicitly to a project version, instance, Base stage or mapped project extension. Never infer ownership solely from time or current stage.
Retain failed attempts, retries, repairs, multiple instances, multiple chats and pause/resume history. Later versions cannot silently inherit an earlier version's binding.
Unresolved attribution remains explicitly unclassified; incomplete coverage is described as recorded consumption rather than a complete version total.
Provide on-demand in-progress snapshots and durable snapshots after each actual Base-stage completion; extension nodes retain detail and an explicit Base aggregation stage.
A successful publication creates a publication-time cumulative report; closure creates the final report including post-publication work.
Snapshot creation follows committed lifecycle events and is recoverable and idempotent. Reporting failure must not block, fail, redispatch or change the lifecycle or release.
Reports fix a cutoff/source ledger position; late data creates a new report revision and preserves prior reports. Aggregate raw ledger records, never add cumulative reports together.
Show stage/current-version totals and shares, plus project/Target/task, work type, model and main/subagent detail. These are views of one ledger, not additive totals.
Ship native installed CLI/HTTP MCP and Runtime Expert entries with Markdown and JSON output, and disclose unavailable Host capabilities precisely.
exclusions: Harness or Ontology integration for statistics
Parent-project Expert, statistics implementation or new parent version
Currency/cost estimation, budget gates, quality/efficiency scores or automatic optimization
New statistics Dashboard or additional page
Runtime LLM profile/provider, model secrets or autonomous Agent execution
Automatic access to all chats or unrelated local files
Changing publisher Base stages, existing release authority or historical acceptance results

cases.expected: Inclusive input/output and cached/reasoning subset semantics normalize without duplicate addition.
Missing metrics/coverage remain null or partial; no fabricated zero or complete total.
Cumulative replay and out-of-order observations do not duplicate or subtract recorded consumption.
Source reset/new epoch and correction retain evidence and do not invent negative consumption.
Fork inheritance is excluded from new work; actual main/subagent usage remains separately attributable.
Explicit project/version/instance/stage/task/attempt bindings reject scope drift and unknown instance references.
Cross-chat reconnect and pause/resume preserve one version ledger and original source cursors.
Multiple instances, retries, failures and repair attempts all retain their consumption exactly once.
Concurrent tasks use explicit attribution; current stage or wall-clock proximity cannot reassign them.
Project extension details map explicitly to Base report stages without changing the Base or runtime gates.
Cutoff snapshots and late-data revisions remain immutable; totals derive from source ledger entries.
An active stage supports native on-demand partial or complete-as-declared usage reports.
Each of the eight actual Base stage completions produces its own idempotent snapshot.
Actual publication success produces the publication-time cumulative report.
Actual closure produces a final report including subsequent closure work and no unrelated later version.
Reporting interruption/failure recovers without changing stage outcomes, resetting budgets or redispatching CI.
Stage/work-type/task/model views reconcile with the same ledger, preserve unclassified records and do not sum percentages across views.
Main/subagent and model/provider details retain source provenance; unavailable model fields remain unknown.
Actual Codex Host source events are collected by the installed native adapter, with cumulative/last-turn semantics and capability limits verified.
Read-only source registration rejects path/symlink/credential/prompt leakage and does not scan unrelated chats.
All exposed entries enforce project/current principal scope; revocation prevents further collection or disclosure as applicable.
Restart, backup/restore and supported upgrade preserve source offsets, deduplication, bindings and report history.
Exact installed CLI, HTTP MCP and actual Runtime Expert return consistent Markdown/JSON reports using native product code.
Downloaded release and current Codex installation collect real usage and read back reports; original E21/E22 remain independently required.

acceptance.note: These are engineering acceptance obligations for this new Runtime feature, never statistical report success gates on a consuming project's lifecycle. Original 64 groups/22 scenarios/664 instances are preserved; these 24 additive instances have their own ledger.
